description: Free OG image generator: type a title, pick a layout, download a 1200×630 PNG that stays readable when Facebook, LinkedIn, X and Slack crop it.
answer: An OG image generator makes the picture that appears when your page is shared. Type a title and subtitle, pick a theme and layout, add a logo if you like, and download a 1200×630 PNG — drawn in your browser and laid out to stay readable when platforms crop it.

body:
## Open Graph Image Generator: Layouts That Survive Cropping

Platforms don't show your image the same way. Facebook and LinkedIn use a wide 1.91:1 frame; Slack shows a small thumbnail; some messaging apps crop closer to square. A layout that only works at full size loses its headline everywhere else.

So the generator keeps text inside a central safe area and away from the edges, scales long titles down to three lines, and puts the brand at the bottom where a crop is least likely to cut it.

## What makes a good OG image?

One idea, readable at thumbnail size:

1. **A short headline** — six to ten words. Long titles become unreadable at phone size.
2. **High contrast** — dark text on light, or light on dark; avoid busy photos behind text.
3. **Your brand, small** — a name or logo, not a full-width banner.
4. **Different per page** — a generic logo card for every URL wastes the space.

## What size and format should I export?

1200×630 PNG, which is what this tool produces. [Meta recommends at least 1200×630](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/sharing/webmasters/images/) at a 1.91:1 ratio, and [LinkedIn's minimum is 1200×627](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a521928). PNG keeps text crisp; switch to JPEG only for photo-heavy images that come out large.

That's also what the web has settled on: when we measured the og:image of 270 big-brand homepages in October 2026 ([dataset](/resources/technical-seo-baseline-2026-10.json)), the median width was 1200 pixels and PNG was the most common format, 166 of 270.

## How do I add it to my page?

Upload the PNG and reference it in your page head, ideally with its dimensions:

```
<meta property="og:image" content="https://yoursite.com/og/page.png">
<meta property="og:image:width" content="1200">
<meta property="og:image:height" content="630">
```

Then confirm it loads and crops well with the [OG image checker](/tools/og-image-checker), and generate the rest of your tags with the [meta tag generator](/tools/meta-tag-generator).

faqs.a: The image named in a page's og:image tag. Facebook, LinkedIn, X, Slack, Discord and messaging apps show it in the preview card when someone shares the link.

faqs.q: Is this OG image generator free?
faqs.a: Yes. It runs entirely in your browser with no signup, no watermark and no upload — the PNG is created on your device and downloaded directly.

faqs.q: Can I generate OG images automatically for every page?
faqs.a: Yes, with code. Frameworks such as Next.js can render OG images per page at build or request time. This tool is for designing the template or making images by hand.
